courses.name: Financial Accounting
outcomes: Understand the theoretical framework of accounting as well as accounting standards.
Demonstrate the ability to prepare financial statements of manufacturing and non-manufacturing sole proprietors.
Work out the accounting treatments for consignment transactions in the books of consignor and consignee.
Understand the accounting treatment for royalty transactions and articulate royalty agreements.
Demonstrate accounting treatments for dependent and independent branches.

modules.title: Theoretical Framework of Accounting
topics: Meaning, scope, objectives, importance and functions of accounting
Terminologies; users of accounting information; accounting process
Cash basis and accrual basis; branches of accounting
Concepts, conventions, Accounting Standards and Ind AS (theory)
Accounting equation — theory and problems

modules.title: Financial Statements of Sole Proprietary Concerns
topics: Manufacturing, trading and profit & loss accounts and balance sheet of manufacturing and non-manufacturing entities
Problems on final accounts of sole proprietors

modules.title: Consignment Accounts
topics: Consignor and consignee; goods invoiced at cost and at selling price
Normal loss, abnormal loss, valuation of stock, stock reserve
Journal entries and ledger accounts in the books of the consignor (problems)

modules.title: Royalty Accounts
topics: Lessee, lessor, minimum rent, short workings, recoupment
Accounting in the books of the lessee only, including minimum-rent account
Sub-lease and lessor books excluded

modules.title: Branch Accounts
topics: Objectives of branch accounting; dependent, independent and foreign branches
Debtors system — ascertainment of branch profit or loss (problems)

skillActivities: Collect annual financial statements of a sole proprietor and identify concepts/conventions used.
Prepare a pro-forma invoice and account sales with imaginary figures.
Prepare a royalty table with imaginary figures.
Prepare a branch account with imaginary figures.
references: S. Anil Kumar, V. Rajesh Kumar and B. Mariyappa — Financial Accounting, Himalaya
S.N. Maheshwari and S.K. Maheshwari — Financial Accounting, Vikas
B.S. Raman — Financial Accounting Vol. I & II
Robert N. Anthony, David Hawkins, Kenneth A. Merchant — Accounting: Text and Cases, McGraw-Hill

outcomes: Bring out the relevance of F.W. Taylor's view on management in today's knowledge era.

Fourteen principles of management

modules.title: Planning

Decision-making process; SWOC analysis

sampleQuestions.subject: Financial Accounting
sampleQuestions.text: State the accounting equation. Name any two users of accounting information.
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Users: owners, management, lenders, tax authorities, employees, investors.

sampleQuestions.subject: Financial Accounting
sampleQuestions.text: Ind AS in Indian corporate reporting are converged with:

options.text: The Companies Act schedule of 1956 exclusively

sampleQuestions.explanation: Indian Accounting Standards are substantially converged with IFRS.

sampleQuestions.subject: Financial Accounting
sampleQuestions.text: From imaginary figures of a sole-proprietor manufacturer, outline the order of statements: Statement of Manufacture → Trading A/c → P&L A/c → Balance Sheet. Where does opening work-in-progress appear?
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Opening WIP is debited on the Statement of Manufacture (or manufacturing account); closing WIP is credited there. Finished goods opening/closing appear on the Trading Account.

sampleQuestions.subject: Financial Accounting
sampleQuestions.text: Distinguish normal loss and abnormal loss in consignment. How is each treated in valuing unsold stock?
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Normal loss (evaporation, leakage) is expected and its cost is borne by remaining units — stock is valued after inflating unit cost. Abnormal loss is credited to consignment (and often transferred to P&L / insurance); it is not loaded onto closing stock.

sampleQuestions.subject: Financial Accounting
sampleQuestions.text: Define minimum rent and short workings. When can short workings be recouped?
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Minimum rent is the guaranteed amount payable to the lessor even if actual royalty is lower. Short workings = minimum rent − actual royalty. They are recouped in later years if the agreement allows, from excess of royalty over minimum rent, within the recoupment period.

sampleQuestions.subject: Financial Accounting
sampleQuestions.text: What is the debtors system of branch accounting? Which branches is it suitable for?
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Under the debtors system the head office treats the dependent branch like a debtor: goods sent, remittances, expenses and returns are recorded in a Branch Account whose balance after closing stock/petty cash is the branch profit or loss. Suitable for dependent branches that do not keep full double-entry books.

sampleQuestions.subject: Management Principles and Applications
sampleQuestions.text: List any five of Fayol's fourteen principles of management.
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Division of work; authority and responsibility; discipline; unity of command; unity of direction; subordination of individual interest; remuneration; centralisation; scalar chain; order; equity; stability of tenure; initiative; esprit de corps (any five).

sampleQuestions.subject: Management Principles and Applications
sampleQuestions.text: What is SWOC analysis? Write one illustration each of a strength, weakness, opportunity and challenge for a Bengaluru degree college.
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: SWOC = Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Challenges (a planning tool in the BCU module). Example: S — experienced faculty; W — limited lab hours; O — NEP/SEP skill courses and internships; C — fee competition from neighbouring colleges. (Accept SWOT.)

sampleQuestions.subject: Principles of Marketing
sampleQuestions.text: Need, want and demand are related as:

options.text: Demand is a want backed by purchasing power
Need is created only by advertising

sampleQuestions.explanation: Needs are basic; wants are culturally shaped; demand = want + ability and willingness to pay.

sampleQuestions.subject: Principles of Marketing
sampleQuestions.text: Sketch the four stages of the product life cycle and name one marketing objective at each stage.
sampleQuestions.modelAnswer: Introduction — create awareness / induce trial. Growth — maximise market share. Maturity — defend share, differentiate. Decline — harvest or withdraw. Sales and profit curves should be mentioned.
